interior.definition: a. situated within or suitable for inside a building\ns. inside and toward a center\ns. of or coming from the middle of a region or country
interior.translation: n. 内部, 内政\na. 内部的, 心灵的, 内地的, 内政的

examples.en: He made over the interior of his house.
examples.zh: 他把屋子重新装修了。

intermediate.definition: n. a substance formed during a chemical process before the desired product is obtained\na. lying between two extremes in time or space or state
intermediate.translation:
n. 中间物, 调停者, 中级
a. 中间的, 中级的
vi. 起媒介作用
[计] 中级

examples.en: My level in English is intermediate.
examples.zh: 我英文水平中等。

internal.definition: a. happening or arising or located within some limits or especially surface\ns. occurring within an institution or community
internal.translation: a. 内在的, 国内的\n[医] 内的, 内部的

examples.en: The button battery in the PC's internal timer has gone flat.
examples.zh: 电脑内部计时器内的纽扣电池没电了。

international.definition: n. any of several international socialist organizations\na. concerning or belonging to all or at least two or more nations
international.translation: a. 国际的\nn. 国别设定\n[计] 国别设定

examples.en: The international language Ido was born in 1907 in Paris, France.
examples.zh: 国际语言伊多语于 1907 年诞生于法国巴黎。

examples.en: Putin will be a pariah on the international stage.
examples.zh: 普丁将成为国际舞台上的弃儿。

examples.en: International problems must be solved by diplomacy, not war.
examples.zh: 国际问题必须靠外交而非战争解决。

internet.definition: n. a computer network consisting of a worldwide network of computer networks that use the TCP/IP network protocols to facilitate data transmission and exchange
internet.translation: [计] 因特网, 国际互连网, 网际网络, 互连网络, 广域网

examples.en: Connecting a PC to the internet is not rocket science.
examples.zh: 将电脑连线到网际网路并不是什么难事。

examples.en: In fact, there are countless, varied uses for the Internet.
examples.zh: 实际上，网络的作用有着无数的多种多样的。

examples.en: For computer people, days are like years without the internet.
examples.zh: 对计算机人员来说，断网的时候度日如年。

interpret.definition: v. make sense of; assign a meaning to\nv. give an interpretation or rendition of
interpret.translation: vt. 解释, 演出, 翻译, 理解\nvi. 翻译, 解释

examples.en: How do you interpret these words?
examples.zh: 这几个字该怎么解释？

examples.en: I interpreted her silence as a refusal.
examples.zh: 我认为她的沉默就是表示拒绝。

examples.en: The same sign may be interpreted differently by different people or different cultures.
examples.zh: 同一个符号，不同的人或不同的文化可能会有不同的解读。

interpretation.definition: n. a mental representation of the meaning or significance of something\nn. an explanation that results from interpreting something\nn. an explanation of something that is not immediately obvious
interpretation.translation: n. 解释, 演出, 翻译\n[计] 插值; 插值法; 解释

examples.en: Your interpretation is based merely on the surface meaning.
examples.zh: 你的理解有点望文生义了。

examples.en: Your interpretation is a bit too literal.
examples.zh: 你的理解有点望文生义了。

examples.en: It is subject to interpretation.
examples.zh: 这件事靠个人的立场来解释。

interrupt.definition:
n. a signal that temporarily stops the execution of a program so that another procedure can be carried out
v. make a break in
v. destroy the peace or tranquility of
v. interfere in someone else's activity
interrupt.translation:
vt. 中断, 妨碍, 插嘴
vi. 打断
n. 中断
[计] 中断

examples.en: Tom didn't want to interrupt Mary while she was studying.
examples.zh: Tom不想在Mary读书时骚扰她。

examples.en: I will try not to interrupt you while you are studying.
examples.zh: 我会尽量不打扰你复习。

examples.en: Please don't interrupt me while I'm talking.
examples.zh: 我说话的时候请你不要插嘴。

interval.definition: n. a set containing all points (or all real numbers) between two given endpoints\nn. the distance between things\nn. the difference in pitch between two notes
interval.translation: n. 间隔, 距离, 间歇, 间隙\n[计] 时间间隔

examples.en: There was a long interval before he replied.
examples.zh: 他间隔了很久才作答。

examples.en: It's best to go to the dentist at regular intervals.
examples.zh: 最好定期去看牙医。

examples.en: The Olympic Games take place at intervals of four years.
examples.zh: 每隔四年，奥运会举行一次。

intervene.definition: v. get involved, so as to alter or hinder an action, or through force or threat of force\nv. be placed or located between other things or extend between spaces and events\nv. occur between other event or between certain points of time
intervene.translation: vi. 插入, 调停, 干涉\n[经] 进场干预

examples.en: We take health for granted until illness intervenes.
examples.zh: 我们视健康为理所当然, 直到疾病侵袭。

intervention.definition: n. the act of intervening (as to mediate a dispute, etc.)\nn. a policy of intervening in the affairs of other countries\nn. (law) a proceeding that permits a person to enter into a lawsuit already in progress; admission of person not an original party to the suit so that person can protect some right or interest that is allegedly affected by the proceedings
intervention.translation: n. 插入, 介入, 调停\n[经] 干预

examples.en: We could only hope for the intervention of higher powers.
Preparations for a military intervention are in their final stages.
We are not equipped for such kind of intervention.

interview.definition:
n. the questioning of a person (or a conversation in which information is elicited); often conducted by journalists
v. conduct an interview in television, newspaper, and radio reporting
v. discuss formally with (somebody) for the purpose of an evaluation
v. go for an interview in the hope of being hired
interview.translation: n. 面谈, 访问, 接见, 面试\nvt. 接见, 对...进行面谈(试)

examples.en: You'll have to play it by ear at the interview.
examples.zh: 在面试的时候你必须见机行事。

examples.en: I reminded him of his interview with the president.
examples.zh: 我提醒他要去会见总裁。

examples.en: I've got my college interview tomorrow. Hopefully I'll pass.
examples.zh: 明天就要去入学面试了，希望可以通过。

intimate.definition:
v. give to understand
s. marked by close acquaintance, association, or familiarity
s. involved in a sexual relationship
s. thoroughly acquainted through study or experience
intimate.translation: a. 亲密的, 私人的, 秘密的\nvt. 暗示, 通知, 告诉\nn. 至交

examples.en: We're intimate friends.
examples.zh: 我们是亲密的朋友。

intimidate.definition: v. make timid or fearful\nv. to compel or deter by or as if by threats
intimidate.translation: vt. 威胁, 恐吓\n[法] 恐吓, 威胁, 使恐惧

examples.en: Don't try to intimidate me.
examples.zh: 别想吓唬我。

examples.en: Tom didn't seem to be intimidated.
examples.zh: 汤姆似乎没有被吓到。

examples.en: She wasn't intimidated by him.
examples.zh: 她并不畏惧他。

into.definition:
prep. To the inside of; within. It is used in a variety of
   applications.
prep. Expressing entrance, or a passing from the outside of a
   thing to its interior parts; -- following verbs expressing motion; as,
   come into the house; go into the church; one stream falls or runs into
   another; water enters into the fine vessels of plants.
prep. Expressing penetration beyond the outside or surface, or
   access to the inside, or contents; as, to look into a letter or book;
   to look into an apartment.
prep. Indicating insertion; as, to infuse more spirit or
   animation into a composition.
prep. Denoting inclusion; as, put these ideas into other words.
prep. Indicating the passing of a thing from one form,
   condition, or state to another; as, compound substances may be resolved
   into others which are more simple; ice is convertible into water, and
   water into vapor; men are more easily drawn than forced into
   compliance; we may reduce many distinct substances into one mass; men
   are led by evidence into belief of truth, and are often enticed into
   the commission of crimes'into; she burst into tears; children are
   sometimes frightened into fits; all persons are liable to be seduced
   into error and folly.
into.translation: prep. 进入...之内, 朝..., 深入...之中, 成为...状况

examples.en: A fall into a pit, a gain in your wit.
examples.zh: 吃一堑，长一智。

examples.en: As soon as I left home, I ran into her.
examples.zh: 我一离开家就遇见了她。

examples.en: The insect grew out of a pupa into an imago.
examples.zh: 昆虫破蛹而出变成成虫。

intricate.definition: s. having many complexly arranged elements; elaborate
intricate.translation: a. 复杂的, 错综的, 缠结的, 难懂的

examples.en: Great thoughts are created through intricate details.
examples.zh: 细节成就伟大的想法。

intrigue.definition: n. a crafty and involved plot to achieve your (usually sinister) ends\nn. a clandestine love affair\nv. cause to be interested or curious
intrigue.translation: n. 阴谋, 复杂的事\nvi. 密谋, 私通\nvt. 激起...的兴趣, 用诡计取得

examples.en: Foreign people intrigue me.
examples.zh: 外国人很有意思。

intrinsic.definition: a. belonging to a thing by its very nature\ns. situated within or belonging solely to the organ or body part on which it acts
intrinsic.translation: a. 本质的, 原有的, 真正的\n[医] 内部的, 内在的

examples.en: This celebration is an intrinsic part of the culture of our country.
I question the intrinsic value of nihilism.
Tom lacks intrinsic motivation to study French.

introduce.definition:
v. cause to come to know personally
v. bring something new to an environment
v. bring in or establish in a new place or environment
v. bring before the public for the first time, as of an actor, song, etc.
introduce.translation: vt. 介绍, 引入, 采用, 输入\n[法] 引进, 输入, 介绍

examples.en: I think the time is right to introduce this product.
examples.zh: 我觉得现在是发表这个产品的好时机。

examples.en: I would like to introduce you to my wife.
examples.zh: 让我向您介绍我的妻子。

examples.en: Now I want to introduce my parents to you.
examples.zh: 现在我要向你介绍我的父母。

introduction.definition:
n. the act of beginning something new
n. the first section of a communication
n. a basic or elementary instructional text
n. a new proposal
introduction.translation: n. 介绍, 传入, 采用, 初步

examples.en: Could you give us a brief introduction of yourself?
examples.zh: 你能简短地介绍一下你自己吗？

examples.en: Mr Gilmore is so well known as to need no introduction.
examples.zh: Gilmore先生如此有名，就不必介绍了。

examples.en: I came to work here though his introduction.
examples.zh: 通过他的介绍，我来到这里工作。

intrude.definition: v. enter uninvited\nv. search or inquire in a meddlesome way\nv. thrust oneself in as if by force
intrude.translation: vi. 闯入, 侵入\nvt. 强加于

examples.en: Reporters do not hesitate to intrude into people's privacy.
examples.zh: 记者没有犹豫地去干涉了人们的私生活。

examples.en: Take care not to intrude upon her privacy.
examples.zh: 注意不要侵犯她的隐私。

examples.en: I didn't mean to intrude.
examples.zh: 我无意打扰。

intuition.definition: n. instinctive knowing (without the use of rational processes)\nn. an impression that something might be the case
intuition.translation: n. 直觉, 直觉的知识

examples.en: By intuition he knew she was lying.
examples.zh: 他凭直觉发现她在撒谎。

invade.definition: v. march aggressively into another's territory by military force for the purposes of conquest and occupation\nv. occupy in large numbers or live on a host\nv. penetrate or assault, in a harmful or injurious way
invade.translation: vt. 侵入, 拥入, 侵略, 侵袭\n[法] 强入, 侵犯, 侵略

examples.en: People shouldn't be allowed to invade countries whose names they can't pronounce correctly.
examples.zh: 人们不应该侵犯自己读不正确名字的国家。

examples.en: All oil-rich countries should be invaded and annihilated by US forces to protect their civilian populations and teach them democracy.
examples.zh: 所有石油资源丰富的国家都应该被美国军队入侵并摧毁，以保护那里的平民并向他们传授民主。

invalid.definition:
n. someone who is incapacitated by a chronic illness or injury
v. force to retire, remove from active duty, as of firemen
a. having no cogency or legal force
s. no longer valid
invalid.translation: n. 病人, 残废者\na. 有病的, 无效的

examples.en: My credit card was invalid.
examples.zh: 我的信用卡无效。

invaluable.definition: s. having incalculable monetary, intellectual, or spiritual worth
invaluable.translation: a. 无价的, 价值无法衡量的

examples.en: The Internet is an invaluable source of information.
examples.zh: 互联网是一种无法估量的信息资源。

examples.en: His help has been invaluable.
examples.zh: 他的援助真是雪中送炭。

invasion.definition: n. the act of invading; the act of an army that invades for conquest or plunder\nn. any entry into an area not previously occupied\nn. (pathology) the spread of pathogenic microorganisms or malignant cells to new sites in the body
invasion.translation: n. 侵犯, 侵入, 侵害\n[医] 侵袭, 侵入, 发病

examples.en: Tatoeba: As if the geek invasion wasn't enough.
examples.zh: Tatoeba:好像怪客入侵还不够似的。

invent.definition: v. come up with (an idea, plan, explanation, theory, or principle) after a mental effort
invent.translation: vt. 发明, 创作, 虚构\n[机] 发明

examples.en: Children were apt to invent their own games.
examples.zh: 孩子们总爱创作自己的游戏。

examples.en: Don't use "discover" when you mean "invent".
examples.zh: 当你在指「发明」的时候，不要用「发现」这个字。

examples.en: The first lute was invented during the Qin dynasty.
examples.zh: 最早的琵琶大约在秦朝时期发明的。

invention.definition: n. the creation of something in the mind\nn. a creation (a new device or process) resulting from study and experimentation\nn. the act of inventing
invention.translation: n. 发明, 创作能力, 虚构的故事\n[经] 发明

examples.en: This invention was the result of years of patient experiment.
examples.zh: 这发明是多年来耐心实验的成果。

examples.en: The invention of the transistor marked a new era.
examples.zh: 晶体管的发明标志著一个新时代的开始。

examples.en: Intel gets a huge royalty from the invention.
examples.zh: 英特尔公司由那个发明取得着巨大的专利权收入

inventory.definition:
n. a detailed list of all the items in stock
n. (accounting) the value of a firm's current assets including raw materials and work in progress and finished goods
n. making an itemized list of merchandise or supplies on hand
v. make or include in an itemized record or report
inventory.translation: n. 详细目录, 存货清单\nvt. 列入详细目录, 清点存货\n[计] 存货清单

examples.en: Keep an inventory of the pantry's contents to avoid over-purchasing.
As a warehouse worker, Carlos is responsible for inventory management.
Tom rearranged the items in his inventory to make more space.

invest.definition: v. make an investment\nv. furnish with power or authority; of kings or emperors\nv. provide with power and authority
invest.translation: vt. 投资, 花费, 笼罩, 授予\nvi. 投资, 利用

examples.en: Don't be afraid to invest time and energy.
examples.zh: 不要害怕付出。

examples.en: The company invested a lot of money in this project.
examples.zh: 该公司在这个企划中投入了很多钱。

examples.en: The government should invest more money in agriculture.
examples.zh: 政府应该加大对农业的投资。

investigate.definition: v. investigate scientifically\nv. conduct an inquiry or investigation of

examples.en: Investigate thoroughly the bushes where the enemy may be hiding.
examples.zh: 仔细搜寻敌人可能藏身的灌木丛。

examples.en: He announced that he would come at once and investigate the matter.
examples.zh: 他宣布他将立刻来调查此事。

examples.en: A committee was constituted to investigate prices.
examples.zh: 为了调查物价，成立了一个委员会。

investigation.definition: n. the work of inquiring into something thoroughly and systematically
investigation.translation: n. 调查, 审查\n[医] 调查, 调查研究

examples.en: The report proved true as a result of their investigation.
examples.zh: 他们的调查结果显示这篇报导是真实的。

examples.en: The reporter elaborated on the method of his investigation.
examples.zh: 报告者详尽地说明了他的研究方法。

examples.en: It is clearly shown in Johnson's investigation that passive smoking is very harmful.
examples.zh: 在Johnson的调查里，明确地证明了二手烟是很有害的。

investment.definition:
n. money that is invested with an expectation of profit
n. the commitment of something other than money (time, energy, or effort) to a project with the expectation of some worthwhile result
n. outer layer or covering of an organ or part or organism
n. the act of putting on robes or vestments
investment.translation: n. 投资\n[医] 包埋料, 围模料, 包埋法, 围模法

examples.en: In our opinion, solar panels are a good investment.
examples.zh: 在我们看来，太阳能电池是一项很好的投资。

examples.en: They obtained a yield of 8 percent on their investment.
examples.zh: 他们在这次的投资中得到百分之八的收益。

examples.en: Algeria should become China's main investment hot spot in the Mediterranean region.
examples.zh: 阿尔及利亚应该成为中国在地中海地区的主要投资热点。

investor.definition: n. someone who commits capital in order to gain financial returns
investor.translation: n. 投资者\n[经] 投资者

examples.en: She is not the founder, she's the investor.
examples.zh: 她不是创办人，她是投资人。

examples.en: The investor stole the capital of his client.
examples.zh: 投资者把他客户的资金窃取了.

examples.en: Foreign investors withdrew their money from America.
examples.zh: 外国投资者从美国收回他们的钱。

invisible.definition: a. impossible or nearly impossible to see; imperceptible by the eye
invisible.translation: a. 看不见的, 无形的\n[经] 无形的, 表面上看不见的, 未列在公开帐目的

examples.en: If I were invisible I wouldn't have to dress myself.
examples.zh: 若我是隐形的，就不用穿衣服了。

examples.en: If I were invisible, I wouldn't have to wear anything.
examples.zh: 若我是隐形的，就不用穿衣服了。

examples.en: The moon is invisible behind the clouds.
examples.zh: 在云的遮蔽下无法见到月亮。

invitation.definition: n. a request (spoken or written) to participate or be present or take part in something\nn. a tempting allurement
invitation.translation: n. 邀请, 请柬, 引诱\n[经] 邀请, 招待, 吸引

examples.en: It is very impolite of her to decline our invitation.
examples.zh: 她拒绝我们的邀请很不礼貌。

examples.en: If I were free, I would accept your invitation.
examples.zh: 如果我当时有空，我一定会应邀的。

examples.en: Many people rejected the invitation to the welcome party.
examples.zh: 许多人拒绝了欢迎会的邀请。

invite.definition:
n. a colloquial expression for invitation
v. increase the likelihood of
v. invite someone to one's house
v. ask someone in a friendly way to do something
invite.translation: vt. 邀请, 请求, 引起, 招致\nn. 邀请

examples.en: We wish to invite Peter to Japan in the near future.
examples.zh: 我们希望在不久的将来邀请彼得去日本。

examples.en: I'd like to invite you to the party.
examples.zh: 我想请你参加派对。

examples.en: Did you invite her to spend Christmas here?
examples.zh: 你邀请她来这里过圣诞节了吗？

invoke.definition: v. cite as an authority; resort to
invoke.translation: vt. 祈求, 恳求, 实行, 援引, 引起\n[计] 调用; 请求

examples.en: Could the US invoke NATO's Article 5 to attack North Korea?
How do we invoke a response from the computer?
Once Tom tried to invoke a demon, and he almost succeeded.

involve.definition:
v. connect closely and often incriminatingly
v. engage as a participant
v. contain as a part
v. occupy or engage the interest of
involve.translation: vt. 包括, 使陷于, 潜心于, 包围\n[医] 累及, 牵涉, 包含

examples.en: I don't want to be involved in this affair.
examples.zh: 我可不想卷入这场纷争中去。

examples.en: I don't want to be involved in that matter.
examples.zh: 我不想被牵扯到这件事里。

examples.en: Whichever way we choose will involve danger.
examples.zh: 不管我们选哪条路，都会有危险。

involvement.definition: n. a connection of inclusion or containment
involvement.translation: n. 卷入, 牵连, 包含, 困窘\n[经] 财政困难, 经济上的困窘

examples.en: Edmundo doesn’t want Rima to know about his involvement.
Said Chemakh denied any involvement with that Paris-based terrorist organization.
The taxi driver has an involvement in the robbery.

inward.definition: a. relating to or existing in the mind or thoughts\nr. toward the center or interior
inward.translation: a. 内心的, 向内的, 本来的\n[医] 向内的

examples.en: Remember to keep pot handles turned inward on the stove.
The Japanese are often criticized for being inward looking.
Those who look outward dream, but those who look inward awaken.

iron.definition:
n. a heavy ductile magnetic metallic element; is silver-white in pure form but readily rusts; used in construction and tools and armament; plays a role in the transport of oxygen by the blood
n. a golf club that has a relatively narrow metal head
n. implement used to brand live stock
n. home appliance consisting of a flat metal base that is heated and used to smooth cloth
iron.translation: n. 铁, 熨斗, 铁器, 坚强, 烙铁, 镣铐\nvt. 烫平, 熨, 用铁包\nvi. 烫平

examples.en: Iron the inside of collars first, and then the outside.
examples.zh: 先熨烫领子的里面，然后是外面。

examples.en: I cannot iron my clothes. I have no iron.
examples.zh: 我没法烫我的衣服，我没有熨斗。

examples.en: They tried to pry the lock open with an iron bar.
examples.zh: 他们试图用一根铁棒撬开锁。

ironic.definition: s. characterized by often poignant difference or incongruity between what is expected and what actually is
ironic.translation: a. 冷嘲的, 挖苦的, 反话的, 讽刺的, 令人啼笑皆非的, 出乎意料的

examples.en: Does he mean that seriously, or is he being ironic?
I'm not sure if this is ironic or not.
Doesn't that name seem ironic to you: "Holy Army"?

irony.definition: n. incongruity between what might be expected and what actually occurs\nn. a trope that involves incongruity between what is expected and what occurs
irony.translation: n. 反语, 讽刺, 具有讽刺意味的事

examples.en: Writer Luiz Fernando Veríssimo, a columnist capable of uniting generations of readers with irony, precision and sensitivity, died in Porto Alegre, Brazil.
examples.zh: 作家路易斯・费尔南多・沃瑞西莫在巴西阿雷格里港去世，他是位专栏作家，能以讽刺、精确、敏感的文笔团结几代读者。

irrational.definition: a. not consistent with or using reason\na. real but not expressible as the quotient of two integers
irrational.translation: n. 无理数\na. 无理性的, 不合理的

examples.en: Nomophobia is the irrational fear of being without one's phone.
Mark's behavior in the workplace is so irrational and destructive.
Tom has an irrational hatred of the French language.

irregular.definition:
n. merchandise that has imperfections; usually sold at a reduced price without the brand name
a. contrary to rule or accepted order or general practice
s. not occurring at expected times
a. (used of the military) not belonging to or engaged in by regular army forces
irregular.translation: n. 不规则物, 不合规格之物\na. 不规则的, 不整齐的, 不合法的

examples.en: I don't like learning irregular verbs.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢学习不规则动词。

irrelevant.definition: a. having no bearing on or connection with the subject at issue
irrelevant.translation: a. 不恰当的, 无关系的, 不相干的\n[法] 无关的, 不相干的, 离题的

examples.en: Sometimes I find that I basically have no time to pay attention to irrelevant trivia.
examples.zh: 有时候发现自己基本上没有时间顾及一些无关紧要的琐事。

irrigate.definition: v. supply with a constant flow or sprinkling of some liquid, for the purpose of cooling, cleansing, or disinfecting
irrigate.translation: vt. 灌溉, 冲洗伤口, 使清新\nvi. 灌溉

examples.en: Some vineyards still choose to irrigate using underground water sources.
Canals have been built to irrigate the desert.
They need to be able to irrigate without relying solely on rain.

irritate.definition: v. excite to an abnormal condition, or chafe or inflame\nv. excite to some characteristic action or condition, such as motion, contraction, or nervous impulse, by the application of a stimulus
irritate.translation: vt. 激怒, 使发怒, 使兴奋, 使发炎\nvi. 引起不快

examples.en: If someone irritates you, it is best not to react immediately.
examples.zh: 如果有人激怒你，你最好不要立刻做出反应。

examples.en: Tom said that he was irritated.
examples.zh: 汤姆说他很烦躁。

island.definition: n. a land mass (smaller than a continent) that is surrounded by water\nn. a zone or area resembling an island
island.translation: n. 岛, 岛屿, 孤立地区, 安全岛\nvt. 使成岛状, 孤立

examples.en: We will deliver up to the airport of the island.
examples.zh: 我们将移交至岛上的机场。

examples.en: Viewed from a distance, the island looked like a cloud.
examples.zh: 这个岛从远方看起来像一片云。

examples.en: Thanks to the favorable wind, we soon reached the island.
examples.zh: 多亏了顺风，我们很快就到了那个小岛。

isolate.definition: v. place or set apart\nv. obtain in pure form\nv. separate (experiences) from the emotions relating to them
isolate.translation: vt. 使隔离, 使孤立, 使绝缘\nn. 隔离种群

examples.en: Several cottages have been isolated by the flood water.
examples.zh: 好几间小屋被洪水孤立起来了。

isolation.definition:
n. a state of separation between persons or groups
n. a feeling of being disliked and alone
n. the act of isolating something; setting something apart from others
n. (psychiatry) a defense mechanism in which memory of an unacceptable act or impulse is separated from the emotion originally associated with it
isolation.translation: n. 隔绝, 孤立, 隔离\n[化] 分离; 生物分离

examples.en: The millionaire lived in complete isolation from the outside world.
Patients with coronavirus need to be kept in isolation.
The theme of isolation features prominently in his work.

issue.definition:
n. an important question that is in dispute and must be settled
n. one of a series published periodically
n. the act of providing an item for general use or for official purposes (usually in quantity)
n. supplies (as food or clothing or ammunition) issued by the government
issue.translation: n. 发行, 问题, 后果, 流出, 出口, 争端\nvi. 发行, 流出, 造成...结果, 传下\nvt. 使流出, 放出, 发行, 发布, 发给

examples.en: I don't know how she should deal with that issue.
examples.zh: 不知道她应该怎么处理那个问题。

examples.en: Don't dodge the issue, I want you to answer my question.
examples.zh: 不要逃避，我要你回答我的问题。

examples.en: We have different ways of thinking with regard to this issue.
examples.zh: 关于这一点，我的想法和你不同。

item.definition: n. a distinct part that can be specified separately in a group of things that could be enumerated on a list\nn. a whole individual unit; especially when included in a list or collection\nr. (used when listing or enumerating items) also
item.translation: n. 项目, 条款, 一则, 项\n[计] 项

examples.en: The first item he bought was an alarm clock.
examples.zh: 他买的第一项东西是一个闹钟。

examples.en: I called customer service because they sent me the wrong item.
examples.zh: 我给客服打电话，因为他们给我寄错货了。

examples.en: He donated a large pile of items to the museum.
examples.zh: 他将一大堆东西捐赠给博物馆。

ivory.definition: n. a hard smooth ivory colored dentine that makes up most of the tusks of elephants and walruses
ivory.translation: n. 象牙, 乳白色\na. 象牙制的, 乳白色的

examples.en: The economist and statistician based in Ivory Coast says commercial trade in the region is primarily conducted with France.
examples.zh: 这位常驻科特迪瓦的经济学家兼统计学家表示，该地区的商业贸易主要与法国进行。

iceberg.definition: n. a large mass of ice floating at sea; usually broken off of a polar glacier
iceberg.translation: n. 冰山, 冷冰冰的人

examples.en: The sea looked quite green, and large icebergs were floating about.
examples.zh: 海水看起来一片碧绿，巨大的冰山漂浮在周围。

examples.en: "Tom chopped up the manuscript like it was iceberg lettuce." "Sounds brutal." "It was, but it was also necessary."
examples.zh: 「汤姆像切卷心莴苣一样，把手稿切碎了。」「听起来很残忍。」「没错，而且也没有那个必要。」

icon.definition: n. (computer science) a graphic symbol (usually a simple picture) that denotes a program or a command or a data file or a concept in a graphical user interface\nn. a conventional religious painting in oil on a small wooden panel; venerated in the Eastern Church
icon.translation: n. 画像, 肖像, 偶像, 图标, 像标\n[计] 像标, 图标

examples.en: You have added a comment, not a translation. To add a translation, click on the "あ→а" icon above the sentence.
examples.zh: 您已添加了评论，而不是一个翻译。要添加一个翻译，点击这句话上面的«あ→а»图标。

ignite.definition: v. cause to start burning; subject to fire or great heat
ignite.translation: vt. 点燃, 使灼热, 使兴奋

examples.en: This could ignite an arms race between Algeria and Morocco.
What you wish to ignite in another must burn inside you.
Politicians ignite the war flame, and the idiots do the rest.

illicit.definition: a. contrary to accepted morality (especially sexual morality) or convention
illicit.translation: a. 不法的, 不正当的, 禁止的\n[法] 违法的, 违禁的, 被禁止的

examples.en: The Anglosphere and Europe consume most of the world's illicit drugs.
It's illicit to have sex outside of marriage.
Sami was too involved in an illicit relationship.

immaculate.definition: s. completely neat and clean\ns. free from stain or blemish
immaculate.translation: a. 无污点的, 纯洁的, 无缺点的, 无辜的\n[医] 无斑点, 无瑕疵的, 洁净的

examples.en: Much as I hate to admit it, his mullet is immaculate.
She cleans the house endlessly, thus keeping it immaculate.
Skura is running an immaculate household in Algiers.

impasse.definition: n a situation in which no progress can be made or no advancement is possible\nn a street with only one way in or out
impasse.translation: n. 难局, 僵局, 死路, 死胡同

examples.en: Here contemporary particle physics is pretty much at an impasse.
Has the war in Ukraine reached an impasse?
We had our priorities, they had their preferences, and we came to an impasse.

impede.definition: v. be a hindrance or obstacle to
impede.translation: vt. 妨碍, 阻碍, 阻止

examples.en: A lack of motivation can impede your language learning progress.
Obstructions near doors can impede people in an emergency.
I hope it doesn't impede my online classes.

impending.definition: v be imminent or about to happen\ns close in time; about to occur
impending.translation: a. 即将发生的, 迫切的, 悬空的\n[法] 就要来的, 逼在眼前的, 紧急的

examples.en: Agitated activity by certain animals may be a sign of an impending earthquake.
examples.zh: 某些动物烦躁不安, 可能是地震临震前的预兆。

impoverish.translation: vt. 使贫穷, 耗尽...的力气

examples.en: More than 75% of them fear that technology impoverishes the traditional French language.
examples.zh: 他们其中的 75 ％ 以上都担心技术导致传统法语的衰落。

improvise.definition: v. perform without preparation\nv. manage in a makeshift way; do with whatever is at hand
improvise.translation: vt. 即席创作, 临时做

examples.en: They improvised most of their lines.
examples.zh: 他们的台词大部分都是即兴发挥的。

impunity.definition: n. exemption from punishment or loss
impunity.translation: n. 不受惩罚, 无事, 无患\n[法] 不受刑罚, 免罚, 免罪

examples.en: In Iraq, American mercenaries had total impunity to kill.
War criminals should not benefit from amnesty or impunity.
The occupying forces commit all sorts of crimes with absolute impunity.

inanimate.definition: a. belonging to the class of nouns denoting nonliving things\na. not endowed with life
inanimate.translation: a. 失去知觉的, 没生命的, 无精打采的\n[医] 无生命的, 无生机的

examples.en: Stop threatening inanimate objects, they can't hear you.
The spirits can be good or evil and can inhabit inanimate objects.

incarcerate.definition: v lock up or confine, in or as in a jail
incarcerate.translation: vt. 下狱, 监禁, 禁闭\n[法] 监禁, 使下狱, 禁闭

examples.en: If we incarcerate these old men, we can take control.
Mennad took car of Baya's affairs while she was incarcerated.
Daniel was incarcerated for thirty-five years in that correctional institution.

increment.definition: n a process of becoming larger or longer or more numerous or more important\nn the amount by which something increases
increment.translation: n. 增加, 增值, 盈余\n[计] 增量

examples.en: The small increment made no impact on the projection.
There are a lot of challenges now due to the increment of prices.
Every time you go through the cycle, you increment the counter by one.

incubate.definition: v. grow under conditions that promote development
incubate.translation: vt. 孵, 培养, 使发展\nvi. 孵蛋, 潜伏, 筑巢, 孵化, 酝酿\nn. 孵育物

examples.en: The hens incubate her eggs untill they hatch.
You will have to incubate the eggs artificially.
The female then incubates the clutch of two pinkish eggs.

inept.definition: s. revealing lack of perceptiveness or judgment or finesse
inept.translation: a. 不适当的, 不理智的, 笨拙的\n[法] 不称职者, 无能的, 不符要求的

examples.en: I am inept at getting along with the women.
They are a bunch of inept and aggressive cretins..
I'm not usually this inept.

inertia.definition: n. (physics) the tendency of a body to maintain its state of rest or uniform motion unless acted upon by an external force
inertia.translation: n. 惯性, 惰性, 迟钝\n[化] 惯性

examples.en: He continued to live as if by inertia.
She continued to live as if by inertia.
Inertia is inherent in any material object.

infancy.definition: n. the early stage of growth or development\nn. the earliest state of immaturity
infancy.translation: n. 幼年, 初期, 幼儿期\n[医] 婴儿期(一足岁以内)

examples.en: Space science is still in its infancy.
examples.zh: 空间科学还在起步阶段。

infantry.definition: n. an army unit consisting of soldiers who fight on foot

examples.en: The twelfth infantry regiment suffered great losses during this skirmish.
The infantry soldier is only a pawn in the game of war.
Dan studied psychological warfare techniques at infantry academy.

influx.definition: n the process of flowing in
influx.translation: n. 流入, 河口, 汇集\n[医] 注入, 流入

examples.en: When will Algeria enjoy an influx of foreign manufacturers?
Initial readings indicate an influx of toxic chemicals.
The influx of foreign workers has caused a serious housing problem in this area.

inhibition.definition: n. (psychology) the conscious exclusion of unacceptable thoughts or desires\nn. the quality of being inhibited\nn. (physiology) the process whereby nerves can retard or prevent the functioning of an organ or part
inhibition.translation: n. 禁止, 抑制, 压抑\n[计] 禁止

examples.en: Tom is truly free from inhibition.
She's prepared to argue without inhibition.
He made her drink to lower her inhibitions.

inmate.definition: n. one of several resident of a dwelling (especially someone confined to a prison or hospital)
inmate.translation: n. 同住者, 被收容者\n[法] 内部的, 接近中心的, 内在的

examples.en: On the 20th of January 2025, the inmates took over the asylum.
examples.zh: 2025 年 1 月 20 日，精神病患接管了精神病院。

innate.definition: a not established by conditioning or learning\ns being talented through inherited qualities\ns present at birth but not necessarily hereditary; acquired during fetal development
innate.translation: a. 先天的, 天生的\n[医] 先天的, 生来的

examples.en: He has an innate love of adventure.
examples.zh: 他天生热爱冒险。

inoculate.definition: v. introduce an idea or attitude into the mind of\nv. introduce a microorganism into\nv. insert a bud for propagation
inoculate.translation: vt. 接种, 嫁接\n[医] 接种

examples.en: None of the family had been inoculated against diphtheria.
It was discovered that less than one child in a hundred had been inoculated against endemic disease.

inquisitive.definition: s. showing curiosity\ns. inquiring or appearing to inquire
inquisitive.translation: a. 好问的, 想知道的, 好追根究底的

examples.en: She is inquisitive, but I like her none the worse.
Climbing the ramp, she felt someone's inquisitive gaze on her.
Sometimes cats' inquisitive personalities get the best of them.

insidious.definition: s. beguiling but harmful\ns. intended to entrap\ns. working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way
insidious.translation: a. 隐伏的, 阴险的, 狡猾的\n[医] 隐袭的

examples.en: Ziri came up with an insidious idea.
This is a rare and insidious disease.
We are working against an enemy who is very insidious in his methods.

insomnia.definition: n. an inability to sleep; chronic sleeplessness
insomnia.translation: n. 失眠症\n[医] 失眠[症]

examples.en: Ziri has suffered from insomnia since he was a teenager.
While Grumpy couldn't sleep due to insomnia, Sleepy had narcolepsy.
Please tell me how I can cure my insomnia.

instigate.definition: v provoke or stir up\nv serve as the inciting cause of
instigate.translation: vt. 教唆, 怂恿, 煽动\n[法] 教唆, 煽动, 怂恿

examples.en: It was Tom who instigated me to do it.
They used every means in their power to instigate the people against him.
The Algerian army colonized Kabylia and instigated terror in the villages.

insulate.definition: v. protect from heat, cold, or noise by surrounding with insulating material
insulate.translation: vt. 使绝缘, 隔离\n[医] 绝缘

examples.en: The old home was very draughty and not well insulated.
I want to buy a good quality, insulated basement window.
Can a worm-infested wooden house be insulated against heat loss?

intercept.definition: n. the point at which a line intersects a coordinate axis\nv. seize on its way
intercept.translation: n. 截取, 妨碍, 截距\nvt. 拦截, 阻止, 截取

examples.en: The ship moved into position to intercept the space probe.
The Americans intercepted a German communique during the XYZ Affair.
Is Israel's Iron Dome suddenly incapable of intercepting Hamas missiles?

interim.definition: n. the time between one event, process, or period and another\ns. serving during an intermediate interval of time
interim.translation: a. 暂时的, 临时的, 间歇的\nn. 过渡时期

examples.en: It was only supposed to be an interim solution.
In the interim, please send all communications to Tom.
Abdelkader Bensalah is just the interim president of Algeria.

intermittent.definition: s. stopping and starting at irregular intervals
intermittent.translation: a. 间歇的, 断断续续的\n[化] 间歇的; 间断的

examples.en: Tom tried intermittent fasting, but died of complications soon after.
Intermittent flashes of lightning illuminated the dark gloom of the forest.
Tom is doing intermittent fasting to lose weight.

interrogate.definition: v. transmit (a signal) for setting off an appropriate response, as in telecommunication\nv. pose a series of questions to
interrogate.translation: vt. 质问, 讯问, 审问\nvi. 质问, 讯问

examples.en: I was aware they would interrogate me.
He was interrogated so much that he finally confessed.
Right after my arrest I was interrogated several times.

intuitive.definition: s. spontaneously derived from or prompted by a natural tendency\ns. obtained through intuition rather than from reasoning or observation

examples.en: Your methodical approach contrasts with my intuitive way of problem-solving.
The layout of this app is not very user-friendly or intuitive.
I know English on an intuitive level.

inundate.definition: v. fill or cover completely, usually with water
inundate.translation: vt. 浸水, 泛滥, 淹没, 使充满

examples.en: Fadil's Facebook page was quickly inundated with messages of support.
These days, people are inundated with images, from television and the Web.
The basement of his house is constantly inundated with inexplicable water leaks.

irate.definition: s. feeling or showing extreme anger
irate.translation: a. 发怒的, 生气的

examples.en: How would you deal with an angry or irate customer?
How would you deal with an irate customer?
Layla became very irate with Sami.

isle.translation: n. 小岛, 群岛\nvt. 使成为岛状\nvi. 住在岛屿上

examples.en: They were marooned on a desert isle.
examples.zh: 她们被抛弃在一座荒岛上。

itinerary.definition: n an established line of travel or access\nn a guidebook for travelers\nn a proposed route of travel
itinerary.translation: n. 旅程, 旅行指南, 游记\na. 巡回的, 旅程的

examples.en: Everyone agrees to stay here for the night and make long-term itinerary decisions tomorrow.
examples.zh: 大家同意先在这里住一晚，行程的事情明天再从长计议。

inflame.definition: v. cause inflammation in\nv. arouse or excite feelings and passions\nv. become inflamed; get sore
inflame.translation: vt. 激怒, 点火, 激起\nvi. 着火, 激动, 发炎

examples.en: He didn't come to work because his throat is inflamed.
Don't scratch your mosquito bite. It'll get inflamed.
If the throat is very inflamed, an antiseptic gargle should be used.

inflict.translation: vt. 施以, 加害, 使承受\n[法] 处, 加, 予以

examples.en: Was it necessary to inflict such a punishment on him?
You should not inflict any injury on others on any account.
Sociopaths rationalize the pain they inflict on others.

intersection.definition: n. a point where lines intersect\nn. a junction where one street or road crosses another\nn. a point or set of points common to two or more geometric configurations
intersection.translation: n. 交集, 十字路口, 交叉点\n[计] 逻辑乘; 与

examples.en: You can get there by crossing the street at the second intersection.
examples.zh: 你从这里过去到那里，穿过第二条横马路就是。

examples.en: Turn right at the next intersection.
examples.zh: 请在下一个十字路口右转。

examples.en: Turn right at the intersection.
examples.zh: 在十字路口右转。

ivy.definition: n. Old World vine with lobed evergreen leaves and black berrylike fruits
ivy.translation: n. 常春藤\na. 学院的, 抽象的

examples.en: The wall is partly covered with ivy.
examples.zh: 墙被常青藤覆盖了一部分。

examples.en: English ivy is a climbing vine.
examples.zh: 西洋常春藤是攀缘藤本植物。

examples.en: Ivy started growing in the garden.
examples.zh: 花园里开始冒出常春藤。

imaginative.definition: s. (used of persons or artifacts) marked by independence and creativity in thought or action
imaginative.translation: a. 想像的, 虚构的

examples.en: He used to be an imaginative boy.
examples.zh: 他曾经是一个富有想像力的男孩。

examples.en: He is a very imaginative writer.
examples.zh: 他是非常有想像力的作家。

indoor.definition: a. located, suited for, or taking place within a building\ns. within doors
indoor.translation: a. 户内的, 室内的

examples.en: Nancy enjoys indoor games.
examples.zh: 南希喜欢室内游戏。

intent.definition: n. the intended meaning of a communication
intent.translation: n. 意图, 含义, 故意\na. 专心的, 决心的, 热心的

examples.en: The only difference between a bad cook and a poisoner is the intent.
examples.zh: 一个差劲的厨师和下毒者唯一的不同在于他们的意图。

examples.en: That wasn't my intent.
examples.zh: 这不是我的初衷。

examples.en: Not far away, screened by the forest, crouched Shiegra, the lioness, intent upon devouring the infant for her evening meal.
examples.zh: 不远处，母狮谢格拉匍匐著，隐匿于林间，正伺机将婴儿吞食，作为她的晚餐。

idealistic.definition: a of or relating to the philosophical doctrine of the reality of ideas\ns of high moral or intellectual value; elevated in nature or style
idealistic.translation: a. 理想主义的, 唯心论的, 唯心主义的, 唯心主义者的

examples.en: It may sound idealistic, but that doesn't necessarily mean it's unrealistic.
Outsiders tend to scoff at Esperanto as an idealistic waste of time.
Tom isn't as idealistic as Mary.

idiomatic.definition: a. of or relating to or conforming to idiom
idiomatic.translation: a. 符合语言习惯的, 惯用的, 有许多习语的

examples.en: Is it more idiomatic if I say it like this?
examples.zh: 这样说是不是更加地道呢？

idiot.definition: n. a person of subnormal intelligence
idiot.translation: n. 白痴, 极蠢之人\n[医] 白痴者, 痴子

examples.en: Do you think I think of myself as an idiot?
examples.zh: 你认为我把自己当傻瓜？

examples.en: Someone who doesn't understand you is not necessarily an idiot.
examples.zh: 一个不懂你的人不一定就是一个笨蛋。

examples.en: Do I sound like an idiot if I talk like this?
examples.zh: 我这么说的话是不是像个傻瓜？

idiotic.definition: s insanely irresponsible\ns incongruous; inviting ridicule\ns having a mental age of three to seven years
idiotic.translation: a. 白痴的, 愚蠢的, 呆头呆脑的

examples.en: It's the most idiotic thing I've seen in my life.
Machines are becoming ever smarter, and people ever more idiotic.
This is the most idiotic thing I've ever heard.

idly.translation: adv. 懒惰地, 空闲地

examples.en: She was idly looking out of the window.
examples.zh: 她无所事事地看向窗外

examples.en: She was looking idly out of the window.
examples.zh: 她无所事事地看向窗外

examples.en: She looked idly out of the window.
examples.zh: 她无所事事地看向窗外

ignition.definition: n. the process of initiating combustion or catching fire\nn. the mechanism that ignites the fuel in an internal-combustion engine\nn. the act of setting something on fire
ignition.translation: n. 点火, 点燃\n[化] 点火; 着火

examples.en: Yuri put the key in the ignition and turned it.
Put the key in the ignition and start the engine.
This car is fully equipped with an ignition interlock device.

illiteracy.definition: n. ignorance resulting from not reading\nn. an inability to read

examples.en: Which is the first illiteracy free village in Bangladesh?
Contractions seems to be a slippery slope towards illiteracy.
The government has made joint efforts to eradicate illiteracy.

illusory.definition: s based on or having the nature of an illusion
illusory.translation: a. 产生幻觉的, 幻影的, 错觉的\n[法] 因错觉产生的, 虚幻的

examples.en: The feelings of "love at first sight" and "faithful unto death" are unrealistic; this sort of unrealistic and illusory feeling is not what we need.
examples.zh: 「一见钟情」以及「从一而终」的感情是不切实际的，我们需要的不是这种不切实际而虚幻的感情。

imaging.definition: n. (medicine) obtaining pictures of the interior of the body

examples.en: A number of imaging techniques are employed in radiology, such as X-ray, MRI, and ultrasound.
examples.zh: 放射学中采用了数种影像技术，比如 X 光、MRI 和超音波。

immersion.definition: n. a form of baptism in which part or all of a person's body is submerged
immersion.translation: n. 沉浸, 专心, 陷入\n[医] 浸, 浸渍

examples.en: He needed a Berber language immersion course.
examples.zh: 他需要参加柏柏尔语沉浸式课程。

immigrate.definition: v. migrate to a new environment\nv. introduce or send as immigrants\nv. come into a new country and change residency
immigrate.translation: vt. 使移居入境\nvi. 移入

examples.en: When did you immigrate to our country?
examples.zh: 你何时移民到我们国家?

impatience.definition: n. a restless desire for change and excitement\nn. a dislike of anything that causes delay
impatience.translation: n. 性急, 难耐, 焦急, 急躁

examples.en: I often feel a sense of impatience during family gatherings.
The audience showed their impatience by stamping of feet.
I don't take kindly to pushiness or impatience.

impetus.definition: n a force that moves something along\nn the act of applying force suddenly
impetus.translation: n. 动力, 推动力, 动量\n[医] 冲动, 动能, 起始(病)

examples.en: If there's no reward, what's the impetus to return their dog?
What's the impetus underlying all of your actions?
What gave you the impetus to change?

imposition.definition: n. the act of imposing something (as a tax or an embargo)\nn. an uncalled-for burden
imposition.translation: n. 征收, 课税, 强加, 欺骗\n[经] 征税, 税, 税款

examples.en: Is to reason and to be mistaken, an imposition?
I wouldn't want to be an imposition.
He doesn't like impositions.

impromptu.definition: n. an extemporaneous speech or remark\nn. a short musical passage that seems to have been made spontaneously without advance preparation
impromptu.translation: n. 即席演出, 即兴曲\na. 即席的\nadv. 即席

examples.en: I called a few friends and we had an impromptu party.
It usually takes me more than three weeks to prepare a good impromptu speech.
A musician friend of mine gave an impromptu performance of a piece he had just finished composing.

inborn.definition: s present at birth but not necessarily hereditary; acquired during fetal development\ns normally existing at birth

examples.en: One's success in life has little to do with one's inborn gift.
Linguistic competence is inborn, not acquired.

incidentally.definition: r. of a minor or subordinate nature
incidentally.translation: adv. 伴随地, 偶然, 顺便

examples.en: Incidentally, I have to tell you something.
examples.zh: 我得顺便给你讲件事。

inclined.definition: a. (often followed by `to') having a preference, disposition, or tendency\na. at an angle to the horizontal or vertical position
inclined.translation: a. 倾向于...的, 想要...的, 可能的, 趋向于...的

examples.en: Old people are inclined to look back on the past.
He is inclined to make light of his father's advice.
The Romans were civilized, but were also inclined to debauchery.

inclusion.definition: n. the state of being included\nn. the relation of comprising something\nn. the act of including
inclusion.translation: n. 包含, 内含物\n[计] 蕴含

examples.en: We want to achieve accessibility and inclusion for all.
We use the symbol “⊂” to denote proper inclusion.
How to achieve accessibility and inclusion for everyone?

incumbent.definition:
n. the official who holds an office
s. lying or leaning on something else
s. necessary (for someone) as a duty or responsibility; morally binding
s. currently holding an office
incumbent.translation: a. 现任的, 依靠的, 负有义务的\nn. 领圣俸者, 在职者

examples.en: The company was established in 1950 by the incumbent chairman.
His speeches resemble the straight-to-the-point style of his incumbent.
It is incumbent on you to do so.

indebted.definition: s. owing gratitude or recognition to another for help or favors etc\ns. under a legal obligation to someone
indebted.translation: a. 负债的, 受惠的\n[法] 负债的, 法律上有义务偿还的

examples.en: I'm deeply indebted to you for doing me this favour.
I'm deeply indebted to my friends for all their help.
I am in no small degree indebted to him.

indefinite.definition: a. vague or not clearly defined or stated\ns. not decided or not known
indefinite.translation: a. 模糊的, 不确定的, 无限的\n[法] 不确定的, 无限制的

examples.en: The union went out on a strike for an indefinite period.
In Esperanto there is no indefinite and only one definite article.
These plans have been put on indefinite hold.

indict.definition: v. accuse formally of a crime
indict.translation: vt. 起诉, 控告, 指控\n[法] 控告, 揭发, 对...起诉

examples.en: The grand jury decided not to indict the police officer.
In the absence of sufficient proof, the police could not indict him.
Sami was indicted for the murder of Layla Bakir.

indictment.definition: n. a formal document written for a prosecuting attorney charging a person with some offense\nn. an accusation of wrongdoing
indictment.translation: n. 起诉, 控告, 起诉状\n[经] 起诉书

examples.en: It is unlikely that this indictment will lead to his deportation.
The family name fell into disrepute following their son's federal indictment.
Did you read the indictment?

indifference.translation: n. 不重视, 无兴趣, 漠不关心\n[法] 中立, 不偏袒, 不重视

examples.en: He doesn't have the indifference typical of people from big cities.
examples.zh: 在他身上没有大城市人的那种冷漠。

examples.en: She assumed an air of indifference.
examples.zh: 她假装不在意。

indulgent.definition: a. characterized by or given to yielding to the wishes of someone\ns. tolerant or lenient\ns. being favorably inclined
indulgent.translation: a. 纵容的, 任性的, 宽容的

examples.en: I suppose we're a little too indulgent to the dog.
Tom gave a little indulgent smile.
Tom is quite helpful, indulgent even.

infinity.translation: n. 无限大, 无限\n[计] 无穷

examples.en: Are we alone in this infinity that is the universe?
I love you infinity to the power of infinity.
Tom spent the day lounging by the infinity pool.

inflate.definition:
v. exaggerate or make bigger
v. fill with gas or air
v. cause prices to rise by increasing the available currency or credit
v. increase the amount or availability of, creating a rise in value
inflate.translation: vt. 使膨胀, 使得意, 使通货膨胀, 使充气\nvi. 充气, 膨胀

examples.en: Tom is inflating a balloon.
examples.zh: 汤姆在吹气球。

infliction.definition: n. an act causing pain or damage
infliction.translation: [法] 处罚, 加刑, 刑罚

informant.definition: n. a person who supplies information
informant.translation: n. 提供消息者, 密告者, 被调查者\n[经] 填报人, 被征询人

examples.en: I have reason to believe Tom is an FBI informant.
I have reason to believe Tom is a federal informant.
Tom confessed to me that he was an informant.

informative.translation: a. 提供消息的, 见闻广博的

examples.en: This is a very informative article.
examples.zh: 这是篇信息量很大的文章。

ingenuity.definition: n. the property of being ingenious
ingenuity.translation: n. 心灵手巧, 精巧, 精巧设计

examples.en: It is nothing that a little persistence and ingenuity can't overcome.
Aside from cameras, Ingenuity carries no scientific instruments.
Gabriel survived using his ingenuity and determination.

inhabitant.definition: n. a person who inhabits a particular place
inhabitant.translation: n. 居民, 居住者\n[医] 居民

examples.en: Brazil has almost 200 million inhabitants.
examples.zh: 巴西的居民快数到2亿。

innovate.definition: v bring something new to an environment

examples.en: Tom doesn't innovate, but he does make good movies.
The company rarely innovated, but frequently copied the competition.
Are you always ready to innovate?

innumerable.definition: s too numerous to be counted
innumerable.translation: a. 无数的, 数不清的

examples.en: I have tried innumerable times to contact him.
examples.zh: 我找过他很多次。

insertion.definition: n. the act of putting one thing into another
insertion.translation: n. 插入, 刊载, 插入物\n[计] 插入

examples.en: If the plug gets dirty, wipe it off with a dry cloth before insertion.
The sternocleidomastoid is used as a landmark for insertion of a central venous catheter.
This is a reaction where charges are transferred by the insertion of ions into a solid host.

insider.definition: n. an officer of a corporation or others who have access to private information about the corporation's operations
insider.translation: n. 内部的人, 权威人士, 知道内情的人\n[经] 熟悉内情者

examples.en: The politician tried to cover up the insider trading.
The hedge fund manager was convicted of insider trading.
Suspicion that this amounts to insider trading has strengthened.

insistent.translation: a. 坚持的, 迫切的

examples.en: Why are you so insistent on going with me?
The children were insistent about our taking them to the movies.
The salesman was insistent to the end.

instantaneous.translation: a. 即时的, 瞬间的, 猝发的\n[机] 瞬时的

examples.en: Globalization brought us the possibility of fast and instantaneous communication.
He knew it was so, with an unaccountable but instantaneous certainty.
Your car's speedometer tells you the car's instantaneous speed, not its average speed.

intangible.definition:
n. assets that are saleable though not material or physical
a. (of especially business assets) not having physical substance or intrinsic productive value
a. incapable of being perceived by the senses especially the sense of touch
s. hard to pin down or identify
intangible.translation: a. 难以明了的, 无形的\n[经] 无形的

examples.en: Above the sea hovered a seagull, intangible as a dream.
"Silent Night" was declared an intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO in 2011.
The tango was added to the Unesco list of intangible cultural heritage in 2009.

intelligible.definition: a. well articulated or enunciated, and loud enough to be heard distinctly
intelligible.translation: a. 可理解的, 易理解的, 纯概念性的

examples.en: Kabyle and Shawi are mutually intelligible to a large extent.
Kabyle, Shawi and Riffian are all mutually intelligible Berber dialects.
Kabyle, Shawi and Riffian are all mutually intelligible Berber variants.

intermediary.definition: n a negotiator who acts as a link between parties
intermediary.translation: n. 仲裁者, 调解者, 媒介物, 中间人\na. 中间的, 媒介的

examples.en: I am an intermediary who introduces business.
Until that day we had spoken only through intermediaries.
The two presidents exchanged phone numbers so they could talk without intermediaries.

interruption.definition: n. some abrupt occurrence that interrupts an ongoing activity
interruption.translation: n. 打扰, 中断, 障碍物\n[医] 间断, 阻断, 中止

examples.en: This pleasant vision was shattered by a most unpleasant interruption.
He showed some annoyance at the interruption of lunch.
It was impossible to watch the movie without interruption.

intimacy.definition: n close or warm friendship\nn a usually secretive or illicit sexual relationship\nn a feeling of being intimate and belonging together
intimacy.translation: n. 亲密, 熟悉, 亲昵行为(言语)\n[法] 亲近的行为, 亲密, 隐私

examples.en: He views intimacy as an important part of their bond.
Yanni and Skura need to build back their emotional intimacy.
That will build emotional intimacy between Yanni and his wife.

intricacy.definition: n marked by elaborately complex detail
intricacy.translation: n. 纷乱, 复杂, 错综

examples.en: Carlos is fascinated by biology and all its intricacies.
The investigator tried to figure out the intricacies of the crime.
Carlos is a musician who loves exploring the intricacies of different genres.

intrinsically.definition: r. with respect to its inherent nature

examples.en: At the time, astronomy was still intrinsically linked to astrology.
I feel when I enter an argument, I can intrinsically see the two sides of the argument.
No circumstance, no purpose, no law whatsoever can ever make licit an act which is intrinsically illicit.

introductory.definition: s. serving to open or begin\ns. serving as an introduction or preface
introductory.translation: a. 介绍的, 引导的, 开端的

examples.en: I have to take an introductory seminar next year.
Write this in the introductory section of your paper.
I would like to volunteer to teach introductory courses.

intruder.definition: n. someone who intrudes on the privacy or property of another without permission
intruder.translation: n. 侵入者, 干扰者, 妨碍者\n[计] 入侵者

examples.en: Alberto ran to try and catch up to the intruder.
Did you get a good look at the intruder?
Lorenzo has no idea how the intruder broke in.

intrusion.definition: n. entrance by force or without permission or welcome\nn. the forcing of molten rock into fissures or between strata of an earlier rock formation\nn. rock produced by an intrusive process
intrusion.translation: n. 闯入, 侵扰\n[医] [向内]突入

examples.en: Let me live my life without your judgment or intrusion.
Pardon the intrusion. My apologies for being late for our meeting.
Sami immediately reported the intrusion to the police.

invader.definition: n. someone who enters by force in order to conquer
invader.translation: n. 侵略者\n[化] 侵入物

examples.en: They defended their country against the invaders.
examples.zh: 他们抵御入侵者，保卫了国家。

invasive.definition: a. relating to a technique in which the body is entered by puncture or incision\na. marked by a tendency to spread especially into healthy tissue
invasive.translation: a. 侵入的, 侵略性的, 攻击性的

examples.en: We humans are the best example of an invasive species.
The cheese gave off a most peculiar, most invasive aroma.
No one is invasive in the house of God.

inversion.definition: n. the layer of air near the earth is cooler than an overlying layer\nn. abnormal condition in which an organ is turned inward or inside out (as when the upper part of the uterus is pulled into the cervical canal after childbirth)\nn. a chemical process in which the direction of optical rotation of a substance is reversed from dextrorotatory to levorotary or vice versa
inversion.translation: n. 倒转, 倒置, 倒装\n[化] 反转; 倒反; 反演; 转化

examples.en: Do I like interrogative inversions?

invert.definition: v. make an inversion (in a musical composition)\nv. reverse the position, order, relation, or condition of
invert.translation:
a. 转化的
vt. 使反转, 使颠倒, 使转化
n. 颠倒的事物
[计] 倒置; 反转

examples.en: Through the lens the image was inverted.
examples.zh: 图像在镜片中呈反向。

examples.en: His upper body looks like it has the shape of an inverted triangle; standing there, he seems extremely handsome!
examples.zh: 他上身长得呈倒三角形，站在那里看上去特帅！

inviting.translation: a. 引人动心的, 有魅力的\n[法] 诱惑人的, 动人心的

examples.en: I'm grateful to you for inviting me to the party.
examples.zh: 谢谢你邀我参加派对。

examples.en: I am grateful to you for inviting me to the party.
examples.zh: 谢谢你邀我参加派对。

examples.en: Thank you for inviting me to the party.
examples.zh: 感谢你请我来参加派对。

irrespective.definition: r in spite of everything; without regard to drawbacks
irrespective.translation: a. 不顾的, 无关的, 没关系的

examples.en: She voted for Mr Nishioka irrespective of party lines.
examples.zh: 她不论党派把票投给了西冈先生。

irritating.definition: s. (used of physical stimuli) serving to stimulate or excite\ns. causing physical discomfort; they can be very painful"
irritating.translation: a. 刺激的, 使愤怒的, 气人的

examples.en: You find it irritating that she chose me, don't you?
People who whisper all the time can be very irritating.
I find it irritating when people talk during concerts.

immunize.definition: v. law: grant immunity from prosecution\nv. perform vaccinations or produce immunity in by inoculation
immunize.translation: vt. 使免疫, 赋予免疫性

examples.en: It is important to immunize children against polio.
As a teenager, I went to Western-religion church with my parents, but my belief in science immunized me.

indicative.definition: a. relating to the mood of verbs that is used simple in declarative statements\ns. (usually followed by `of') pointing out or revealing clearly
indicative.translation: a. 指示的, 象征的, 表示...的\n[经] 指标的

examples.en: Macedonian has four verbal moods: indicative, conditional, imperative, and renarrative.
A high forehead is indicative of great mental power.
In the second-person singular, the perfect active indicative of "laudare" is "laudavisti".

inspector.definition: n. a high ranking police officer
inspector.translation: n. 检查员, 巡视员\n[化] 检查员

examples.en: The suspect told a lie to the inspector.
examples.zh: 那嫌疑犯对侦察官撒了个谎。

examples.en: Tom is a tax inspector.
examples.zh: 汤姆是税务督察。

introspective.definition: a. given to examining own sensory and perceptual experiences
introspective.translation: a. 内省的\n[医] 内省的

examples.en: People talk about interesting and introspective subjects when hiking.
Russian art is often deeply personal and introspective.
The rain makes me strange and introspective.

invariably.definition: r without variation or change, in every case
invariably.translation: adv. 不变化地, 恒定地, 始终如一地

examples.en: Yet you seem to be invariably charming to Dr. Bauerstein!
Such a person invariably expends his physical energy more slowly.
Mary invariably brought more food than she could eat.

irrigation.definition: n. supplying dry land with water by means of ditches etc\nn. (medicine) cleaning a wound or body organ by flushing or washing out with water or a medicated solution
irrigation.translation: n. 灌溉, 冲洗\n[医] 冲洗法, 灌溉

examples.en: Algeria needs to use drip irrigation to improve crop yields.
Algeria needs to encourage the use of proper irrigation techniques.
Deforestation and poor irrigation practices can lead to irreversible desertification.

ice-cream.translation: a. 冰淇淋的, 乳白色的

examples.en: The ice-cream will melt, so I put it in the fridge.
examples.zh: 冰淇淋会融化所以我把它放在冰箱里。

examples.en: Stracciatella ice-cream is nothing but a plain ice-cream with chocolate chips.
examples.zh: 斯特拉恰泰拉冰淇淋只不过是一种添加了巧克力碎的普通冰淇淋。

examples.en: If and only if the ice-cream is vanilla flavour will Xiao Wang eat it.
examples.zh: 当且仅当冰淇淋是香草口味，小王会吃这个冰淇淋。

icy.definition: s. covered with or containing or consisting of ice\ns. shiny and slick as with a thin coating of ice
icy.translation: a. 冰的, 冰冷的, 冷淡的, 滑溜的

examples.en: An icy blast of wind chilled me to the bone.
examples.zh: 冰冷的疾风吹到我骨子里去了。

examples.en: It is hard to keep our balance on icy streets.
examples.zh: 在结冰的街道上我们很难保持平衡。

examples.en: Many accidents resulted from the icy conditions of the road.
examples.zh: 道路结冰导致了很多起事故。

idealism.definition: n. (philosophy) the philosophical theory that ideas are the only reality\nn. impracticality by virtue of thinking of things in their ideal form rather than as they really are
idealism.translation: n. 唯心主义, 观念论, 唯心论, 理想主义

examples.en: The idealism of American bourgeois philosophers is aggressive and warlike.
The difference between materialism and idealism is that materialism works.
His wide-eyed idealism is really starting to get on my nerves.

idleness.translation: n. 懒惰, 闲散, 失业\n[化] 空载

examples.en: Sooner or later, you will regret your idleness.
examples.zh: 你迟早要后悔懒惰。

imitation.definition: n. the doctrine that representations of nature or human behavior should be accurate imitations\nn. something copied or derived from an original\nn. copying (or trying to copy) the actions of someone else
imitation.translation: n. 模仿, 效法, 冒充, 赝品\n[医] 模仿, 仿制, 仿制品

examples.en: What is the difference between imitation and real diamonds?
examples.zh: 假的钻石和真的钻石有甚么分别？

immortal.definition: n. a person (such as an author) of enduring fame\na. not subject to death
immortal.translation: n. 不朽人物, 神仙\na. 永远的, 不死的, 长久的

examples.en: There has never been a savior nor an immortal emperor to rely on.
examples.zh: 从来就没有什么救世主， 也不靠神仙皇帝！

examples.en: No one of us is immortal.
examples.zh: 没有人是不朽的。

examples.en: Mortal enemies are immortal friends.
examples.zh: 不共戴天的敌人是不朽的朋友。

implore.definition: v call upon in supplication; entreat

examples.en: "I implore you not to do this, Jack," she cried.
I implore you not to do this, Tom!
I implore her to remain by my side.

improper.definition: a. not suitable or right or appropriate\ns. not conforming to legality, moral law, or social convention\ns. not appropriate for a purpose or occasion
improper.translation: a. 不合适的, 错误的, 不成体统的, 不道德的\n[法] 不适当的, 不合适的, 不正确的

examples.en: It is highly improper.
examples.zh: 这实在不合适。

impurity.definition: n. worthless or dangerous material that should be removed\nn. the condition of being impure
impurity.translation: n. 杂质, 不洁, 不纯\n[化] 杂质

examples.en: The impurities of the water were visible to the naked eye.
To prevent impurities, make sure to reduce the tallow multiple times.
The pipe has a filter for impurities.

inaccessible.definition: a. capable of being reached only with great difficulty or not at all\ns. not capable of being obtained
inaccessible.translation: a. 难得到的, 难接近的, 难达成的

examples.en: This part of Kabylie is a wild and inaccessible land.
The southern shore of the lake is marshy and inaccessible.
They can't understand, however, how inaccessible these areas are.

inaccurate.translation: a. 错误的, 不准确的\n[化] 不精确

examples.en: The wall clock of the living room is inaccurate.
Our experiment has revealed that his report was inaccurate.
To claim there is an all-encompassing Jewish race would be inaccurate.

inasmuch.definition: adv. In like degree; in like manner; seeing that;\n   considering that; since; -- followed by as. See In as much as, under\n   In, prep.
inasmuch.translation: adv. 因...之故, 在...范围内

incandescent.definition: s. emitting light as a result of being heated\ns. characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance
incandescent.translation: a. 白热的, 闪闪发光的, 辉耀的, 灿烂的\n[医] 白炽的, 白热的

examples.en: Incandescent lights bulbs are still in use to this day.
She was incandescent with joy upon hearing his proposal.
We replaced all incandescent lightbulbs with new energy-saving lightbulbs.

incapable.definition:
a. (followed by `of') lacking capacity or ability
s. not being susceptible to or admitting of something (usually followed by `of')
a. (followed by `of') not having the temperament or inclination for
s. not meeting requirements
incapable.translation: a. 无能力的, 不能的\n[机] 不能行的, 耐不住的

examples.en: I am entirely incapable of accepting this minister's arguments.
examples.zh: 我完全无法接受这位公使的言论。

inch.definition: n. a unit of length equal to one twelfth of a foot
inch.translation: n. 英寸, 身高, 小岛\nvi. 慢慢前进, 慢慢移动\nvt. 使缓慢地移动

examples.en: He was beaten to within an inch of his life.
examples.zh: 他被殴打得快死。

examples.en: Give him an inch and he'll take a yard.
examples.zh: 得寸进尺。

examples.en: We waded into the cold water inch by inch.
examples.zh: 我们一步一步地踏进了冰冷的水里。

incompatible.definition: a. not compatible\na. incapable of being used with or connected to other devices or components without modification\ns. used especially of solids or solutions; incapable of blending into a stable homogeneous mixture
incompatible.translation: a. 不相容的, 不能并存的, 矛盾的\n[化] 不协调

examples.en: These two things are incompatible. Which one do you prefer?
Many rabbis think that Judaism is incompatible with Zionism.
Do you think you and I are incompatible?

incomplete.definition: a. not complete or total; not completed\ns. not yet finished
incomplete.translation: a. 不完全的, 未完成的, 不完善的\n[机] 不完全的

examples.en: The salad is incomplete without olive oil, croutons and nuts.
Certain languages use the imperfect tense to express incomplete actions.
The dictionary is incomplete. It only goes to the letter J.

incorrect.definition: a. not correct; not in conformity with fact or truth\ns. (of a word or expression) not agreeing with grammatical principles
incorrect.translation: a. 不正确的\n[法] 不正确, 错误的, 不适当的

examples.en: I'm afraid this is an incorrect formulation of the question.
examples.zh: 恐怕这里提法不妥当。

examples.en: Strictly speaking, this sentence is grammatically incorrect.
examples.zh: 严格地讲,这句话语法上有错误。

examples.en: You have done it totally incorrect!
examples.zh: 你全做错了！

indefinitely.definition: r. to an indefinite extent; for an indefinite time

examples.en: Plans to send humans to Mars had been indefinitely delayed.
You have a tendency to put things off indefinitely.
Some cookies are stored indefinitely on users' hard drives.

indiscriminately.definition: r in a random manner\nr in an indiscriminate manner
indiscriminately.translation: adv. 无差别, 任意地; 不分青红皂白地; 滥; 不分皂白

examples.en: The soldiers indiscriminately fired their guns at the crowd.
Me, I hate people who are indiscriminately friendly.
In May 1945, the French settlers shot Algerians indiscriminately.
In severe weather, it's best to stay indoors.
examples.zh: 天气恶劣的时候尽量不要外出。

examples.en: Catherine stayed indoors because it was raining.
examples.zh: 因为外面正在下雨，所以 Catherine 留在室内。

examples.en: When I was a child, I spent most of my time indoors reading.
examples.zh: 当我是个孩子的时候，我会把大部分时间都用于室内阅读。

induction.definition: n. an electrical phenomenon whereby an electromotive force (EMF) is generated in a closed circuit by a change in the flow of current\nn. the act of bringing about something (especially at an early time)
induction.translation: n. 归纳法, 感应, 就职, 入门\n[计] 归纳法

examples.en: St James Palace represents her, William and his brother Harry, and now regards her "induction" as complete.
examples.zh: 代表她、威廉还有他的弟弟哈利的圣詹姆斯宫现在认为，凯萨琳的“入会时期”已经结束了。

industrialize.definition: v. organize (the production of something) into an industry\nv. develop industry; become industrial
industrialize.translation: vt. 使工业化\nvi. 实现工业化

examples.en: Algeria is trying to industrialize on its own terms.
Japan was the first East Asian country to industrialize.
Britain began to industrialize in the late eighteenth century.

industrious.definition: s characterized by hard work and perseverance\ns working hard to promote an enterprise
industrious.translation: a. 勤勉的, 刻苦的

examples.en: He is an industrious student to the best of my knowledge.
examples.zh: 就我所知，他是个很用功的学生。

examples.en: An industrious person will succeed in life.
examples.zh: 勤劳的人将在生活中获得成功。

examples.en: The Japanese are an industrious people.
examples.zh: 日本人是勤劳的民族。

inefficient.definition: a. not producing desired results; wasteful
inefficient.translation: a. 无效率的, 无能的\n[医] 无效的, 无效力的

examples.en: It is inefficient of you.
examples.zh: 你们的效率太低了。

inevitably.definition: r. in such a manner as could not be otherwise

examples.en: In addition, coincidences inevitably come in threes.
examples.zh: 不但如此，巧合的事还会接二连三地发生。

inexpensive.definition: a relatively low in price or charging low prices
inexpensive.translation: a. 便宜的, 不贵重的

examples.en: Do you know if there's an inexpensive hotel near here?
examples.zh: 您知道这附近有便宜的旅馆吗？

examples.en: Everyone says the food in this restaurant is both delicious and inexpensive.
examples.zh: 大家说这家饭馆儿的菜又好吃又便宜。

infamous.definition: s known widely and usually unfavorably;
infamous.translation: a. 无耻的, 不名誉的, 声名狼藉的

examples.en: After that night they became infamous in the entire city.
While in jail, Tom befriended John, an infamous car thief.
The most infamous expression for the year 2011 is "Kebab murders".

infectious.definition: s. caused by infection or capable of causing infection\na. easily spread; children catch it from their elders"- Bertrand Russell\na. of or relating to infection
infectious.translation: a. 有传染性的, 易传染的\n[医] 传染性的

examples.en: Tom's laughter is infectious.
examples.zh: 汤姆的笑声很有感染力。

inference.definition: n. the reasoning involved in drawing a conclusion or making a logical judgment on the basis of circumstantial evidence and prior conclusions rather than on the basis of direct observation
inference.translation: n. 推论\n[法] 推论, 推理, 推断

examples.en: Type inference has three outputs whereas checking only has two.
Is this an observation or an inference?
Select the statements which are observations rather than inferences.

inferiority.definition: n. the state of being inferior\nn. an inferior quality\nn. the quality of being a competitive disadvantage
inferiority.translation: n. 自卑, 次等\n[医] 下位, 下级, 次级, 劣等

examples.en: How can I rid myself of my inferiority complex?
examples.zh: 我有什么办法可以脱离我的自卑情结吗？

infinitely.translation: adv. 无限地, 无数地, 庞大地

examples.en: How I am is infinitely more important than what I have.
This system of linear equations has infinitely many solutions.
This website is more addicting than Facebook, and infinitely more useful.

infusion.definition:
n. a solution obtained by steeping or soaking a substance (usually in water)
n. the process of extracting certain active properties (as a drug from a plant) by steeping or soaking (usually in water)
n. (medicine) the passive introduction of a substance (a fluid or drug or electrolyte) into a vein or between tissues (as by gravitational force)
n. the act of infusing or introducing a certain modifying element or quality
infusion.translation: n. 注入, 泡制, 注入物\n[化] 浸渍; 浸泡

examples.en: Socrates was sentenced to death by drinking an infusion of poison hemlock.
The Gongfu tea ceremony emphasizes multiple infusions to extract full flavors.
Southern Mongoloids or Sundadonts have infusions of Australoids.
It was much worse than we initially thought.
examples.zh: 事情比我们最初想象的更严重。

examples.en: Initially we had some problems with our computer system, but they've been sorted out now.
examples.zh: 我们的电脑系统起初出了点问题，不过现在已经修理好了。

injure.definition: v. cause injuries or bodily harm to
injure.translation: vt. 伤害, 损害, 使受冤屈\n[医] 损伤

examples.en: You may injure yourself if you don't follow safety procedures.
examples.zh: 如果你不按照安全手续来的话，你可能会受伤的。

examples.en: I heard you were injured trying to help Tom.
examples.zh: 我听说你在试图帮助汤姆的时候受伤了。

examples.en: The ambulances carried the injured to the nearest hospital.
examples.zh: 救护车把伤者送往了最近的医院。

ink.definition:
n. a liquid used for printing or writing or drawing
n. dark protective fluid ejected into the water by cuttlefish and other cephalopods
v. append one's signature to
v. mark, coat, cover, or stain with ink
ink.translation: n. 墨水, 墨汁\nvt. 涂墨水于, 签署, 加墨水

examples.en: She was asked to write her name in ink.
examples.zh: 她被要求用墨水写下她的名字。

examples.en: He gave me a pen that was almost out of ink.
examples.zh: 他给了我一支快没水了的笔。

examples.en: I don't care what color ink, just bring me a pen.
examples.zh: 颜色无所谓，给我一支笔就行了。

inlet.definition: n. an arm off of a larger body of water (often between rocky headlands)
inlet.translation: n. 进口, 插入物\n[化] 入口; 进口; 投料口; 供料口

examples.en: The waters of the inlet were first charted during the eighteenth century.
This inlet is protected from the storms that pass across the open ocean.
This bay produces more shellfish for American tables than any other inlet on the West Coast.

inorganic.definition: a. relating or belonging to the class of compounds not having a carbon basis\na. lacking the properties characteristic of living organisms
inorganic.translation: a. 无机的, 无生物的, 非自然形成的\n[医] 无机的

examples.en: How do organic proteins and nucleic acids emerge from inorganic matter?
How are organic proteins and nucleic acids formed from inorganic matter?
How are organic proteins and nucleic acids created from inorganic matter?

insanity.definition: n. relatively permanent disorder of the mind
insanity.translation: n. 疯狂, 愚顽, 精神错乱\n[医] 精神病

examples.en: Masturbation leads to insanity.
examples.zh: 自慰引发疯狂。

insignificant.definition:
s. not worthy of notice
s. signifying nothing
s. of little importance or influence or power; of minor status
a. devoid of importance, meaning, or force
insignificant.translation: a. 无关紧要的, 无意义的, 琐碎的

examples.en: In itself it was insignificant, but its consequences were vast.
The level of street violence is relatively insignificant in Algeria.
In itself it was insignificant; it had, however, untold consequences.

instability.definition: n. an unstable order\nn. unreliability attributable to being unstable\nn. the quality or attribute of being unstable and irresolute
instability.translation: n. 不安定, 不稳定\n[医] 不稳定性

examples.en: This could create a great deal of instability in Algeria.
The country is going through a period of economic instability.
Gold prices are skyrocketing in the wake of financial instability.

installment.definition: n. a payment of part of a debt; usually paid at regular intervals\nn. a part of a published serial
installment.translation: n. 就职, 装设, 分期付款\n[经] 分期付款

examples.en: I'll be all paid up after one more installment.
I bought this TV on the installment plan.
The payment for the car will be made in 12 monthly installments.

instantly.definition: r without delay or hesitation; with no time intervening\nr without any delay
instantly.translation: adv. 立即地, 即刻地

examples.en: He was hit by a car and died instantly.
examples.zh: 他被车撞了之后便过世了。

examples.en: Tom was hit by a truck and died instantly.
examples.zh: 汤姆被卡车撞到而且当场死亡。

examples.en: Michael instantly got away from Linda.
examples.zh: 麦可立刻从琳达那里逃走了。

instinctively.definition: r. as a matter of instinct
instinctively.translation: adv. 本能地, 直觉地

examples.en: Some teachers instinctively know how to play “favorites” to manipulate the other students.
examples.zh: 有些老师本能地知道怎么去利用“偏心”去控制其他学生。

examples.en: People could not see any hopes of obtaining happiness in this life, thus they instinctively sought comfort in the afterlife.
examples.zh: 人们在此世中看不到任何获得幸福的希望，便很本能地想在彼世中寻求慰藉。

insulator.definition: n. a material such as glass or porcelain with negligible electrical or thermal conductivity
insulator.translation: n. 绝缘体, 从事绝缘工作的工人\n[化] 绝缘体; 绝缘器; 绝缘子; 隔离剂

examples.en: It's a great insulator, keeping hot foods hot and cold foods cold.
Space is actually a good insulator because it is difficult to transfer heat to nothing.

intellectually.translation: adv. 智力上；知性上；理智地

examples.en: My goal is to advance personally and intellectually every day.
Yanni thinks that women are intellectually and physically inferior to men.
Although it leaves much to be desired artistically, intellectually it's very stimulating.

interconnect.definition: v. cause to be interconnected or interwoven

examples.en: Tatoeba is really multilingual. All the languages are interconnected.
examples.zh: Tatoeba确实是多语言的。所有的语言都互相关联。

interface.definition:
n. (chemistry) a surface forming a common boundary between two things (two objects or liquids or chemical phases)
n. (computer science) a program that controls a display for the user (usually on a computer monitor) and that allows the user to interact with the system
n. the overlap where two theories or phenomena affect each other or have links with each other
n. (computer science) computer circuit consisting of the hardware and associated circuitry that links one device with another (especially a computer and a hard disk drive or other peripherals)
interface.translation: n. 分界面, 接触面, 界面\n[计] 接口, 界面

examples.en: I didn't like the interface of that operating system.
examples.zh: 我不喜欢这个操作系统的页面。

examples.en: Please select a language for the Image Viewer interface.
examples.zh: 请为Image Viewer的界面选择语言。

examples.en: The reimagined user interface allows smoother play across devices.
examples.zh: 全新设计的操作介面能让玩家在各种装置上享受更流畅的体验。

intern.definition: n. an advanced student or graduate in medicine gaining supervised practical experience (`houseman' is a British term)\nv. deprive of freedom\nv. work as an intern
intern.translation: n. 实习生, 被拘留者\nvi. 作实习医师(教师、实习生)\nvt. 拘留, 扣留

examples.en: Tomorrow we will welcome the first intern.
examples.zh: 明天我们将迎来第一个实习生。

examples.en: Tom is just an intern.
examples.zh: 汤姆只不过是实习生。

interpreter.definition: n. someone who mediates between speakers of different languages\nn. someone who uses art to represent something\nn. (computer science) a program that translates and executes source language statements one line at a time
interpreter.translation: n. 直译程序, 解释者, 口译者, 注释器\n[计] 注释器

examples.en: She has a strong wish to work as an interpreter.
examples.zh: 她非常想当口译。

examples.en: GCC is a compiler while Python is an interpreter.
examples.zh: Gcc是一个编译器而python是一个解释器。

examples.en: The interpreter tries to give the most detail and information possible.
examples.zh: 翻译正在试图给尽可能多的细节和消息。

intonation.definition: n. rise and fall of the voice pitch\nn. singing by a soloist of the opening piece of plainsong\nn. the act of singing in a monotonous tone
intonation.translation: n. 朗诵, 语调, 唱\n[化] 声调

examples.en: Intonation is very important. It can completely change the meaning.
Written text generally cannot convey the intonation of spoken language.
Pay more attention to intonation when you speak English.

intriguing.definition: s. capable of arousing interest or curiosity
intriguing.translation: a. 吸引人的, 有趣的

examples.en: That is intriguing.
examples.zh: 那真有趣。

inventor.definition: n. someone who is the first to think of or make something
inventor.translation: n. 发明家\n[法] 发明人, 发明家, 创造者

examples.en: I wanted to be an inventor when I was young.
When I was young, I wanted to be an inventor.
Who was the inventor of the telephone, Bell or Meucci?

inverse.definition: n. something inverted in sequence or character or effect\ns. reversed (turned backward) in order or nature or effect\na. opposite in nature or effect or relation to another quantity
inverse.translation: a. 倒转的, 相反的\nn. 反向, 反面\n[计] 反白, 反色

examples.en: The inverse of a non-square matrix is a dangerous thing.
examples.zh: 非方矩阵的逆阵是一个危险的东西。

inversely.definition: r. in an inverse or contrary manner
inversely.translation: adv. 相反地\n[机] 反的, 反对

examples.en: The length of a marriage is inversely proportional to the cost of the wedding.
examples.zh: 婚姻的长度与婚宴的花费负相关。

examples.en: The number of muffins that you'll receive will be inversely proportional to the number of times you talk on IRC.
examples.zh: 你能得到松饼数量将和你去IRC聊天的次数成反比。

invoice.translation: n. 发票, 发货单\nv. 开发票, 记清单

examples.en: They told me there was a problem with the invoice.
Tom admitted he had made a mistake on the invoice.
We paid an invoice of more than one thousand dollars.

ion.definition: n. a particle that is electrically charged (positive or negative); an atom or molecule or group that has lost or gained one or more electrons

examples.en: The computer whose keyboard was bought by Ion was locked.
Lithium ion batteries are used in almost all electric vehicles.
An ion enters a cell through an ion channel.

ironically.definition: r. contrary to plan or expectation\nr. in an ironic manner
ironically.translation: adv. 冷嘲地, 挖苦地, 讽刺地, 令人啼笑皆非地

examples.en: Ironically, the fan shop gets really warm in the summer.
There are certain expressions which are now only used ironically.
Ironically, it was his best friend who arrested him.

irregularity.definition: n. not characterized by a fixed principle or rate; at irregular intervals\nn. an irregular asymmetry in shape; an irregular spatial pattern
irregularity.translation: n. 不规则, 例外, 违反规则的行为\n[化] 不匀度

examples.en: He is the last man to commit an irregularity.
The many irregularities in your language don't really alleviate boredom.
I think your language is just boring. Irregularities don't interest me.
